messages:
maya: dropped an Nsight capture into the thread - seeing a ~120ms all-reduce tail on the last microbatch of pipeline stage B when we switch kernels. link: https://ci.redwood/trace/2187654321 :thinking_face:
liam: looking now. are we on the new autopick path or the fallback kernel?
sasha: my read from similar runs was kernel_autopick -> fallback due to small seq_len penalty. could be batch steering pushing a tiny last microbatch that trips a slow kernel.
olga: pasted the key timeline snippet from nsight (summarized):
```
GPU0: compute kernels uninterrupted until 0.87s, then stall 0.120s during all-reduce
GPU1: starts all-reduce early but waits on recv at 0.86s -> imbalance
Host timers: kvcache_prefetch=9ms, merge_kv=18ms, allreduce_wait=120ms
```
tony: nvprof counters from the same run:
```
Allreduce bytes: 1.2GB
PCIe memcpy: 0.0 (NVLINK active)
Kernel occupancy drop on rank 2 at microbatch 7 -> warp stalls++
Custom timers: comm_overlap=0.03, compute_time=0.48, extra_wait=0.12
```
benchbot: perf-alert: regression detected vs baseline (2179000000). metric: tail_allreduce_latency increased +85ms (p95). pinned diff: kernel_autopick decision changed for model: redwood/llm-ig-2b, seq_len=512, microbatch=8.
maya: interesting that autopick flipped. can someone check kernel selection logs around 0.85-0.87s? maybe quantized path fallback?
liam: found logs: "kernel_selector: chose kernel=matmul_fp16_shard_v2 for parts 0-3, fallback=matmul_generic_fp16 for part 4". part 4 is the smaller partition after uneven split.
sasha: that uneven partition looks like microbatch boundary + cached KV footprint; the kv cache warmup didn't amortize because the small tail batch didn't hit the hot path. batching heuristic should prefer equal partition sizes or pad last batch.
olga: quick experiment: padding last microbatch by 16 tokens removed the fallback in a quick capture and reduced all-reduce tail by ~90ms. no accuracy/regression on sample prompt.
tony: experiment logs attached (short):
```
run: pad_tail=16 -> kernel_autopick stable across ranks, allreduce_wait=28ms, end-to-end lat -0.08s
run: pad_tail=0  -> fallback on rank4, allreduce_wait=122ms
```
maya: nice. sounds like a batching heuristic fix (pad or steer) could be a low-risk mitigation. can we add an autopick guard: prefer uniform partitioning when potential fallback latency > X ms?
liam: yes. will add a patch to kernel_selector: if candidate kernels differ and estimated fallback penalty > 40ms, prefer the variant that keeps partitions balanced. adding unit test + nsight regression capture in CI.
sasha: also add a KVCACHE metric: "kv_warmth_ratio" (cached_tokens / expected_tokens) so we can detect tails that underwarm. benchbot: noted new metric request.
benchbot: scheduled perf-capture job: run/2187654321-padding-experiment -> results ETA 2h. tagging: @devex for rollout notes.
maya: ok next steps: 1) liam patch kernel_selector guard, 2) sasha add pad heuristic + kv_warmth_ratio emit, 3) olga collect nsight capture for the patched path, 4) CI perf run. will triage if this shows up on other models. thanks all :thumbsup:
